facts.statement: The genus Dreadnoughtus was described by Lacovara and colleagues in 2014.
facts.quote: parent_authority: Lacovara et al., 2014

facts.statement: Dreadnoughtus lived during the Late Cretaceous, specifically from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian stages.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Late Cretaceous (Campanian–Maastrichtian),

facts.statement: Two partial skeletons of Dreadnoughtus were found in the Cerro Fortaleza Formation in Santa Cruz Province, Argentina, dating to approximately 76 to 70 million years ago.
facts.quote: It is known from two partial skeletons discovered in Upper Cretaceous (Campanian to Maastrichtian, approximately 76–70 million years ago) rocks of the Cerro Fortaleza Formation in Santa Cruz Province, Argentina.

facts.statement: The immature type specimen of Dreadnoughtus measured 26 meters in length and weighed between 48 and 49 metric tons.
facts.quote: It is one of the largest terrestrial vertebrates known from reasonably complete remains, with the immature type specimen measuring 26 m in total body length and weighing up to 48–49 metric tons (53–54 short tons).

facts.statement: Dreadnoughtus is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod that contains only one species, Dreadnoughtus schrani.
facts.quote: Dreadnoughtus is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur containing a single species, Dreadnoughtus schrani.

facts.statement: American paleontologist Kenneth Lacovara discovered the remains of Dreadnoughtus in 2005 in Patagonia, Argentina.
facts.quote: American palaeontologist Kenneth Lacovara discovered the remains in the Cerro Fortaleza Formation in Santa Cruz Province, Patagonia, Argentina in 2005.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen MPM-PV 1156 includes a partial skeleton with 32 caudal vertebrae, 18 haemal arches, both sternal plates, and various limb elements but lacks the front foot and hind foot.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen, MPM-PV 1156, consists of a partial skeleton, somewhat preserved in its original layout, that comprises: a maxilla (jaw) fragment; a tooth; a posterior cervical vertebra; cervical ribs; multiple dorsal vertebrae and dorsal ribs; the sacrum; 32 caudal vertebrae and 18 haemal arches (bones from the tail) that include a sequence of 17 anterior and middle caudal vertebrae and their corresponding haemal arches found in their original layout; the left pectoral girdle and forelimb minus the front foot; both sternal plates; all pelvic elements; the left hind limb lacking a hind foot and right tibia; metatarsals I and II; and one claw from digit I.

facts.statement: The Dreadnoughtus fossils were returned to the Museo Padre Molina in Rio Gallegos, Argentina, in March 2015.
facts.quote: Dreadnoughtus schrani fossils were returned to their permanent repository at the Museo Padre Molina in Rio Gallegos, Argentina in March 2015.

facts.statement: Researchers used a NextEngine 3D laser scanner to scan the bones of both Dreadnoughtus specimens.
facts.quote: The bones of both Dreadnoughtus specimens were scanned with a NextEngine 3D laser scanner.

facts.statement: Dreadnoughtus provides significant insight into the anatomy of giant titanosaurians, particularly regarding their limbs and shoulder and hip girdles.
facts.quote: The discovery of Dreadnoughtus schrani provides insight into the size and anatomy of giant titanosaurian sauropods, especially of the limbs and the shoulder and hip girdles.

facts.statement: Dreadnoughtus possessed an unusually long neck that made up almost half of its total body length.
facts.quote: Dreadnoughtus also has an unusually long neck for its body size, making up almost half of the animal's length.

facts.statement: The original researchers estimated the Dreadnoughtus type specimen weighed about 59.3 tons using a scaling equation based on limb bone circumference.
facts.quote: The researchers who described Dreadnoughtus schrani estimated its weight using Equation 1 of Campione and Evans (2012), which allows the body mass of a quadrupedal animal to be estimated based only on the circumference of the humerus and femur. Using this scaling equation, they concluded that the Dreadnoughtus type specimen weighed about 59.3 t.

facts.statement: Sauropod researcher Matt Wedel used volumetric models to estimate the Dreadnoughtus weight between 30 and 40 tons.
facts.quote: On SV-POW web blog, sauropod researcher Matt Wedel used volumetric models, based on the published figures, that yielded estimates between 36 - 40 t, or even as low as approximately 30 t, based on a 20% shorter torso.

facts.statement: In 2019, Gregory S. Paul moderated his weight estimate for the Dreadnoughtus type specimen to 31 metric tons.
facts.quote: In 2019, considering the argument of Ullmann and Lacovara (2016), Gregory S. Paul moderated his mass estimate of Dreadnoughtus type specimen at 31 MT, slightly higher than his previous estimation; he even noted that the holotype may have been heavier a tonne or so.

facts.statement: Campione suggested that discrepancies in weight estimates could be due to the immature state of the holotype or unrecognized effects of posture and gait on scaling equations.
facts.quote: Campione suggest this discrepancy could be explained by previously unrecognized effects of posture and gait in the scaling relationship between limb bone circumference and body mass when dealing with animals this large or alternatively, ontogeny, since the holotype of Dreadnoughtus was immature and their scaling equations assume maturity.

facts.statement: Dreadnoughtus lived in South America between 76 and 70 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Dreadnoughtus schrani es la única especie conocida del género extinto Dreadnoughtus de dinosaurio saurópodo titanosaurio que vivió a finales del periodo Cretácico durante el Campaniense al Maastrichtiense, hace 76 a 70 millones de años en lo que es hoy Sudamérica.

facts.statement: The species was first described in 2014 from fossils found in the Cerro Fortaleza Formation in Santa Cruz Province, Argentina.
facts.quote: Fue descrito originalmente en 2014 a partir de restos fósiles de la Formación Cerro Fortaleza de la provincia de Santa Cruz, Argentina.

facts.statement: The single known individual of Dreadnoughtus was estimated to be about 26 meters long and 2 stories tall.
facts.quote: Estimates based on measurements of the known parts of the skeleton suggest that the only known individual of Dreadnoughtus schrani was approximately 26 m long and stood about 2 stories tall.

facts.statement: Its pelvic bone (ilium) measured 1.31 meters in length, which is larger than any other known.
facts.quote: Its ilium, the top bone of the pelvis, is also larger than any other, measuring 1.31 m in length.

facts.statement: The skeleton is 45.3% complete based on the number of bones found out of the estimated total.
facts.quote: 116 bones out of ~256 in the entire skeleton (including the skull) = 45.3% complete

facts.statement: Soft tissues and collagens were discovered in the holotype specimen in 2022.
facts.quote: In 2022, Schroeter and her colleagues discovered soft tissues and collagens from the holotype specimen.

facts.statement: Evidence suggests the holotype specimen was not fully grown when it died.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen was likely not fully grown when it died.

facts.statement: The specimens likely died and were buried quickly during a flood caused by a river levee break.
facts.quote: Based on the sedimentary deposits at the site, the two Dreadnoughtus schrani specimens appear to have been buried quickly during a fluvial avulsion event, or break in a levee resulting in a flood.

facts.statement: Small theropod teeth found near the bones suggest scavenging, possibly by megaraptorans like Orkoraptor.
facts.quote: Numerous small theropod teeth found amongst the bones are likely evidence of scavenging, most likely by megaraptorans, perhaps Orkoraptor.

facts.statement: Paleontologist Kenneth Lacovara compared the animal's gait to that of an Imperial Walker.
facts.quote: Paleontologist Kenneth Lacovara compared the animal's gait to an Imperial Walker.

facts.statement: In the first third of the tail, neural spine bases have cavities caused by contact with air sacs.
facts.quote: In the first third of the tail, the bases of the neural spines are extensively subdivided into cavities caused by contact with air sacs (part of the dinosaur's respiratory system).

facts.statement: The bottom stem of the Y-shaped chevrons is broadly expanded, likely for muscle attachment.
facts.quote: In Dreadnoughtus schrani the bottom stem of the "Y" is broadly expanded, likely for the attachment of muscles.

facts.statement: A subsequent analysis suggested Dreadnoughtus might actually be a lithostrotian closely related to Aeolosauridae.
facts.quote: However, in a subsequent analysis of its limb bones, Ullman & Lacovara found that Dreadnoughtus possessed many of the characteristics of lithostrotians (in particular, it shares a number of traits with Aeolosaurus and Gondwanatitan), which collectively may indicate that it is actually a lithostrotian closely related to Aeolosauridae.

facts.statement: The genus was named by Lacovara and colleagues in 2014.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Lacovara et al., 2014

facts.statement: Most bones of Dreadnoughtus are very well preserved with minimal deformation, especially in the limb bones.
facts.quote: La mayoría de los huesos de Dreadnoughtus schrani están muy bien preservados. Tienen un mínimo de deformación, especialmente en los huesos de las extremidades.

facts.statement: Dreadnoughtus had thin, elongated teeth used for stripping branches from trees.
facts.quote: Como la mayoría de los saurópodos, tenía dientes delgados y alargados para deshojar las ramas arbóreas.

facts.statement: The best-preserved cervical vertebra of Dreadnoughtus measured 1.13 meters in length.
facts.quote: La vértebra cervical mejor preservada medía 1,13 metros de largo

facts.statement: Eight dorsal vertebrae were found in the Dreadnoughtus specimen.
facts.quote: Se hallaron ocho vértebras dorsales

facts.statement: Researchers found almost all of the tail vertebrae, which is rare for titanosaurs.
facts.quote: Los investigadores encontraron casi todas las vértebras de la cola, algo raro en titanosaurios

facts.statement: Fine details, such as vascular markings, are visible on the Dreadnoughtus vertebrae.
facts.quote: Delicados detalles, como las marcas dejadas por el riego vascular, son apreciables en las vértebras de Dreadnoughtus

facts.statement: The scapula of Dreadnoughtus measures 1.74 meters in length.
facts.quote: La escápula mide 1,74 metros

facts.statement: The femur of Dreadnoughtus measures 1.91 meters in length.
facts.quote: Su fémur mide 1,91 metros de largo

facts.statement: Dreadnoughtus is one of the largest dinosaurs known from well-preserved skeletons, estimated at 26 meters long and 12.8 meters high.
facts.quote: Dreadnoughtus schrani es uno de los mayores dinosaurios conocidos por esqueletos bien preservados, siendo estimado con una longitud total de 26 metros y 12,8 metros de alto.

facts.statement: At 1.74 meters, the Dreadnoughtus scapula is longer than any known titanosaur scapula.
facts.quote: Con 1.74 metros, su omóplato es más largo que cualquier otro omóplato de titanosaurio conocido.

facts.statement: The Dreadnoughts ilion measures 1.31 meters, making it larger than any other known.
facts.quote: Su ilion, el hueso superior de la pelvis, también es más grande que cualquier otro, mide 1,31 metros de longitud.

facts.statement: The Dreadnoughtus forearm is longer than any previously known titanosaur forearm.
facts.quote: El antebrazo es más largo que cualquier otro conocido anteriormente de un titanosaurio

facts.statement: Estimates of Dreadnoughtus's weight have been controversial.
facts.quote: Pero la estimación de su peso ha sido tema de controversia.

facts.statement: Initial weight estimates based on femur and humerus circumference reached 59.3 tonnes.
facts.quote: Mediante ecuaciones de regresión, de la circunferencia del fémur y el húmero, se estimó inicialmente con un peso de 59,3 toneladas

facts.statement: Later studies using 3D skeletons and volume estimation methods derived a weight range of 22.1 to 38.2 tonnes.
facts.quote: Pero estudios posteriores, más exhaustivos y directos, creada usando un esqueleto 3D y un método de estimación de volumen de masa, deriva un rango de 22.1-38.2 toneladas.

facts.statement: The maximum estimated mass of Dreadnoughtus is 38.225 tonnes.
facts.quote: Masa máxima 38,225 toneladas

facts.statement: The total length of Dreadnoughtus is estimated at 26 meters.
facts.quote: largo total 26 metros

facts.statement: The head and neck of Dreadnoughtus measure 12.2 meters in length.
facts.quote: Cabeza y Cuello 12,2 metros

facts.statement: The neck of Dreadnoughtus alone measures 11.3 meters in length.
facts.quote: Cuello solamente 11,3 metros

facts.statement: The torso and hip region of Dreadnoughtus measure 5.1 meters in length.
facts.quote: Torso y cadera 5,1 metros

facts.statement: The tail of Dreadnoughtus measures 8.7 meters in length.
facts.quote: Cola 8,7 metros

facts.statement: The shoulder height of Dreadnoughtus is approximately 6 meters.
facts.quote: Altura en el hombro ~ 6 metros

facts.statement: Kenneth Lacovara discovered the remains of Dreadnoughtus in Cerro Fortaleza Formation, Santa Cruz Province, Patagonia, Argentina, in 2005.
facts.quote: El Dr. Kenneth Lacovara , de la Universidad Drexel, descubrió los restos en la Formación Cerro Fortaleza en la Provincia de Santa Cruz, Patagonia argentina, en 2005.

facts.statement: Excavating the complete remains of Dreadnoughtus required four austral summers for the research team.
facts.quote: su equipo requirió cuatro veranos australes para excavar completamente los restos.

facts.statement: In 2009, Dreadnoughtus fossils were shipped by ocean freighter to Philadelphia for preparation and study at the Academy of Natural Sciences of Drexel University and the Carnegie Museum of Natural History.
facts.quote: En 2009, los fósiles fueron transportados a Filadelfia a través de un carguero oceánico, para la preparación y estudio del material en la Academia de Ciencias Naturales de la Universidad Drexel y en el Museo Carnegie de Historia Natural.

facts.statement: The Dreadnoughtus schrani fossil bones are scheduled to be permanently returned to the Padre Molina Museum in Río Gallegos, Argentina.
facts.quote: Las osamentas fósiles de Dreadnoughtus schrani serán prontamente devueltas, de manera permanente, al Museo Padre Molina en Río Gallegos, Argentina.

facts.statement: Dreadnoughtus fossil bones were scanned using 3D laser technology from NextEngine.
facts.quote: Los huesos fósiles de Dreadnoughtus fueron escaneados con láser 3D de NextEngine.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen MPM-PV 1156 is a partial skeleton preserved in original position, including a jaw fragment, tooth, cervical vertebra, ribs, multiple dorsal vertebrae, sacrum, 32 tail vertebrae, 18 hemal arches, tail bones, left shoulder girdle, left forelimb without hand, both sternum plates, all pelvic elements, left hindlimb without foot, right tibia, metatarsals I and II, and a claw from the first digit.
facts.quote: El espécimen holotipo, MPM-PV 1156, consiste de un esqueleto parcial, preservado parcialmente en su disposición original, que incluye: un fragmento del maxilar, un diente, una vértebra posterior cervical; costillas cervicales, múltiples vértebras y costillas dorsales, el sacro, 32 vértebras caudales y 18 arcos hemales, huesos de la cola, que incluyen una secuencia de 17 vértebras caudales anteriores y medias con sus correspondientes arcos hemales en su disposición original, l parte izquierda de la cintura escapular y la extremidad anterior izquierda sin la mano, ambas placas del esternón, todos los elementos pélvicos, la extremidad posterior izquierda sin el pie y la tibia derecha; los metatarsos I y II, y una garra del primer dígito.

facts.statement: The paratype specimen MPM-PV 3546 is a partially articulated postcranial skeleton of a slightly smaller individual found at the same locality as the holotype.
facts.quote: El paratipo, MPM-PV 3546, consiste de un esqueleto postcraneal parcialmente articulado de un individuo algo más pequeño cuyos restos fueron descubiertos en la misma localidad que el holotipo.

facts.statement: The genus name Dreadnoughtus combines the English words 'dread' and 'nought' to mean 'nothing to fear', referencing the massive size of the species.
facts.quote: El nombre del género, Dreadnoughtus, procede del vocablo inglés dreadnought, resultante de unir dread, "miedo", y nought, "nada", que se puede traducir literalmente como "nada de miedo", para denominar a un tipo de acorazado, que son buques de guerra de gran tonelaje, con lo que se alude indirectamente al enorme tamaño de esta especie.

facts.statement: The name Dreadnoughtus also honors two dreadnought battleships, the Rivadavia and the Moreno, that served in the Argentine fleet, paying tribute to the country where the species was discovered.
facts.quote: Adicionalmente el nombre se refiere a los dos dreadnoughts que sirvieron en la flota argentina en la primera mitad del , el Rivadavia y el Moreno, haciendo así homenaje al país en que se descubrió a Dreadnoughtus schrani.

facts.statement: The species name schrani honors American businessman Adam Schran for his support of the research project.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie, schrani, homenajea el nombre del empresario estadounidense Adam Schran por su apoyo al proyecto de investigación.

facts.statement: Dreadnoughtus belongs to the parent group Eutitanosauria.
facts.quote: Parent group: Eutitanosauria

facts.statement: Dreadnoughtus is classified in the class Saurischia.
facts.quote: Class: Saurischia

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Dreadnoughtus is Dreadnoughtus schrani.
facts.quote: Type species: Dreadnoughtus schrani

facts.statement: Dreadnoughtus lived during the Campanian stage, from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: The initial high mass estimate for Dreadnoughtus was quickly criticized, albeit unofficially, by other sauropod researchers.
facts.quote: Este gran cálculo de masa fue rápidamente criticado, aunque extraoficialmente, por otros investigadores de saurópodos.

facts.statement: Matt Wedel used volumetric models to estimate Dreadnoughtus weight between 30 and 40 tons, based on a torso 20% shorter than used in regression equations.
facts.quote: Matt Wedel utilizó modelos volumétricos que arrojaron una estimación mucho menor entre 35-40 toneladas, o incluso tan bajas como aproximadamente 30 toneladas, basado en un torso un 20% más corto.

facts.statement: In June 2015, Karl T. Bates and colleagues published a formal weight revaluation using digital volumetric models, concluding Dreadnoughtus weighed between 22.1 and 38.2 tons, arguing that regression-based estimates implied impossible amounts of soft tissue.
facts.quote: En junio de 2015 se publicó una revaluación formal del peso del animal. En ella, un equipo de investigación dirigido por Karl T. Bates comparó los resultados de la ecuación de escala simple con los resultados encontrados utilizando un modelo digital basado en volumen con diversas cantidades de tejido blando y "espacio vacío" para el sistema respiratorio. Descubrieron que cualquier modelo que usara la estimación de peso basada en escalas hubiera significado que el animal tuviera una cantidad imposible de volumen, grasa, piel, músculo, etc., en capas sobre su esqueleto. Compararon su modelo volumétrico de D. schrani con los de otros saurópodos con esqueletos más completos y estimaciones de masa mejor entendidas para concluir que el espécimen tipo D. schrani debe haber pesado en el rango de 22,1 a 38,2 toneladas.

facts.statement: Lacovara questioned Bates et al.'s methods, arguing that Dreadnoughtus should not be treated as an exception to established mass estimation methods and that the limb bones would be unnecessarily large if the lower mass estimates were correct.
facts.quote: Lacovara cuestionó los métodos utilizados por Bates et al., argumentando que el nuevo estudio trata a Dreadnoughtus como una excepción a métodos bien establecidos de estimación masiva probados en animales vivos, y que los huesos de las extremidades serían innecesariamente grandes si las nuevas estimaciones de masa fueran correctas.

facts.statement: A 2020 study by Alejandro Otero and colleagues used modern bone measurement equations to re-elevate Dreadnoughtus's estimated weight to 50 tons.
facts.quote: Otro estudio, de 2020, de Alejandro Otero y colaboradores, empleando de nuevo técnicas de medición ósea, pero con ecuaciones más modernas, volvió a elevar su peso hasta las 50 toneladas.

facts.statement: A 2014 ontogenetic study by Lacovara et al. indicated that both Dreadnoughtus specimens were immature at death and still growing, which may explain the discrepancies between different mass estimation methods.
facts.quote: El estudio ontogénico de Lacovara et al. de 2014 indicó que los dos especímenes de Dreadnoughtus eran inmaduros, en el momento de sus muertes todavía no habían dejado de crecer, por lo que podría explicar la elevada incongruencia entre los distintos métodos de estimación.

facts.statement: The nearly complete skeleton of Dreadnoughtus justifies volumetric mass estimation, and it has been suggested that the species may be an outlier in mass estimation comparisons.
facts.quote: El estado íntegro del esqueleto de Dreadnoughtus justifica una estimación volumétrica, cuyos resultados son muy distintos a los entregados en las ecuaciones de regresión, se ha sugerido que Dreadnoughtus pudo ser uno de esos valores atípicos.
